support_spans: painful lower-extremity nodules
Cutaneous lesion biopsy: 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification
concepts.why: The presence of painful lower-extremity nodules and 'Ghost cells' in the cutaneous lesion biopsy points to panniculitis, a rare condition associated with pancreatic cancer.

support_spans: Serum lipase >20,000 U/L
Amylase 7,914 U/L
contradict_spans: Cutaneous lesion biopsy: 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification
concepts.why: The elevated serum lipase and amylase levels suggest pancreatitis, but the presence of 'Ghost cells' in the cutaneous lesion biopsy is not typical for chronic pancreatitis.

support_spans: edematous and tender to palpation, with marked synovitis
contradict_spans: Extensive autoimmune and infectious work-up negative (including ANA, RF, CCP, HLA-B27)
concepts.why: The presence of edema, tenderness, and synovitis suggests an inflammatory arthritis, but the negative autoimmune work-up makes rheumatoid arthritis less likely.

support_spans: painful nodules on the anterior shins and inner left thigh
contradict_spans: Cutaneous lesion biopsy: 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification
concepts.why: The presence of painful nodules on the lower extremities is consistent with erythema nodosum, but the biopsy findings are not typical for this condition.

support_spans: Cutaneous lesion biopsy: 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification
contradict_spans: No previous history of gastrointestinal disease or significant family history of rheumatologic conditions or cancer
concepts.why: The presence of 'Ghost cells' in the cutaneous lesion biopsy is consistent with necrobiotic xanthogranuloma, a rare condition that can be associated with various systemic diseases.
It explains the painful lower-extremity nodules and polyarthralgia due to fat necrosis with saponification.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification in the cutaneous lesion biopsy and the connection between pancreatic duct and adjacent vasculature, along with elevated cancer markers, decided it.
